Submission Date: 10/26/2026

documents.text:
Tracy Cohen, Shady Cove, OR.
Re: FERC eComment Request for Deep Green Cook Inlet Data Center. Permit Notice
FERC Docket P-15423 File List

I a US citizen and property owner in Soldotna Alaska, am opposed to development of the DeepGreen Cook Inlet LLC, a recently registered company out of Delaware, who is seeking federal permits to install a hyperscale data center underwater in the Cook Inlet Forelands region offshore of Nikiski.

The DeepGreen data center would become a significant source of noise, disorienting marine
mammals like beluga whales, who depend on sound to communicate, navigate, hunt, and escape predators. Endangered beluga whales must pass through the Cook Inlet Forelands bottleneck to access their feeding and calving grounds seasonally.
NOAA considers noise to be one of the top threats to Cook Inlet beluga recovery. The noise created by DeepGreen’s data center could break beluga whale habitat in two, separating seasonal feeding and
calving grounds.

Generational Alaskan fisheries are too important to gamble against huge untested infrastructure projects that provide speculative benefits to our communities. 
Every salmon that returns to streams North of Nikiski would need to pass through the bottleneck
where DeepGreen proposes to install 66 server hives and more than three hundred tidal turbine generators. There are setnet sites within 3 miles of the proposed data center.

The DeepGreen data center would release copper, a well-known toxin, directly into the habitat of the Cook Inlet salmon population that we depend on for food, jobs, and our identity as Alaskans. Increased water temperatures, especially at slack tide, have the potential to significantly harm
salmon and the aquatic ecosystem as a whole.

The underwater data center could have many serious impacts on marine life, local utility ratepayers, and the entire Cook Inlet ecosystem.

Potential Impacts:
- Underwater noise
- Warming water temperature
- Copper pollution
- Habitat fragmentation
- Ratepayer energy burden

Please put me down as a solid NO in opposition of DeepGreen data center installed in Cook Inlet Alaska. 
Thank you, Tracy E Cohen
